extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policy makers, and stakeholders interested in NIH peer review and grant funding processes
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and empirical measurements relevant to how individual reviewers evaluate NIH grant applications (numeric ratings and written critiques) and how consistent those evaluations are across reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers' ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: How reviewers assign ratings to the applications they review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper examined 43 individual reviewers' ratings of the same 25 NIH grant applications and found no agreement among reviewers regarding application quality, despite all reviewers receiving the same instructions on how to rate applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written critiques format
rubrics_metrics.description: Format and content of reviewers' written critiques accompanying their ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reviewers received the same instructions on how to format their written critiques; nonetheless, reviewers' qualitative critiques did not agree across reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers' qualitative judgments about the strengths and weaknesses of an application (textual critiques).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study compared qualitative evaluations across reviewers of the same applications and found no agreement in these qualitative judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative evaluations / numeric rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers' numeric scores or ratings assigned to applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper analyzed numeric ratings and found no agreement among reviewers; it also examined how reviewers translate qualitative observations (strengths/weaknesses) into numeric ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of strengths and weaknesses into numeric rating
rubrics_metrics.description: How a given number or types of reported strengths and weaknesses are reflected in the reviewer's numeric score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although reviewers reported counts of strengths and weaknesses, the study found no agreement in how reviewers 'translated' a given number of strengths and weaknesses into a numeric rating—i.e., identical counts produced different scores depending on the reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrater agreement measures (e.g., ICC with 95% CIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical measures used to quantify agreement among reviewers examining the same applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper visualizes three measures of agreement among reviewers with 95% confidence intervals and explicitly reports intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs); it notes that observed agreement was effectively zero and that ICC lower bounds are by definition 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of peer review: differentiating top applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation that peer reviewers should distinguish the very best applications from comparatively weaker ones to allocate scarce funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article frames this as the central evaluative purpose of NIH peer review, yet demonstrates empirically that reviewers failed to agree, implying a failure to reliably fulfill that purpose; it also highlights the anti-pattern that outcomes may depend more on which reviewer is assigned than on the research itself.
